title: When the Choir Sings
premise: Yara Underhill, a royal food-taster with the quiet gift of hearing what things truly are, has spent years hiding in plain sight—tasting poison by day and keeping ledgers for the Guild of Impossible Things by night. When the crown declares a hunt for the gifted, her guildmaster betrays the guild's location to buy his own safety, forcing Yara to flee with the one ledger that maps a door out of Vessany—a country that was erased from history decades ago and survives only in memory. Hunted by the Inquisitor Cassian, who once loved her, Yara must decide whether loyalty to her found family outweighs the truth that the door can only be opened by someone who chooses to stay behind. In the end, she gives the ledger to the guild's youngest member and remains as the choir of hidden voices sings the country back into existence—at the cost of her own escape.
about_author: Wren Pemberton is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloging documents from countries that no longer appear on maps. They write fantasy about people whose small, careful work holds collapsing worlds together.

chapters.title: The Taster's Tongue
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. We meet her at the royal table, tasting the king's soup while secretly reading its true nature through her gift, then slipping to the guildhall to balance ledgers of impossible trades. Emotional beat: the comfort of routine and double life, shadowed by her fear of being seen.

chapters.title: A Bell Rung Backward
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The crown proclaims the Purification Edict: all gifted must register or be hunted. The guild scrambles; the guildmaster, Aldous, urges calm while quietly burning records. Emotional beat: dread settling in—the invisible life is ending.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Keeps
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. She discovers the oldest ledger describes the Door of Vessany, an exit from an erased country, openable only by 'a voice that stays.' Cassian, now an Inquisitor, visits the palace and recognizes her. Emotional beat: old love curdling into threat.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Bargain
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Pressured by his superiors, Cassian offers Aldous immunity in exchange for the guild's names. Aldous hesitates—we see his fear and vanity. Emotional beat: betrayal taking root before it blooms.

chapters.title: Ash on the Sill
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Soldiers raid the guildhall at dawn; Yara escapes with the Vessany ledger while members scatter or are taken. She learns Aldous sold them out. Emotional beat: grief and rage; the found family shattered.

chapters.title: Roads Not on Maps
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, joined by Tam, a gifted guild apprentice. They travel toward where Vessany used to be, following the ledger's clues through villages where memory of the country persists in songs. Emotional beat: fragile hope and growing bond with Tam.

chapters.title: The Choir in the Walls
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. In a ruined chapel, they find survivors of Vessany singing the country's name to keep it existing. Tam hears the truth: the Door opens only if one gifted soul remains inside to hold it. Emotional beat: awe turning to horror at the price.

chapters.title: Cassian's Choice
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Ordered to execute captured guild members, he falters, remembering Yara. He lets one prisoner go and is marked for treason himself. Emotional beat: duty cracking against love; he begins hunting the hunt.

chapters.title: The Door of Vessany
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At the border of the erased land, Cassian catches up—not to arrest her but to help. Soldiers close in; Tam cannot work the Door alone. Yara realizes the ledger's meaning: she is the voice that stays. Emotional beat: climax—love, sacrifice, and choice converging.

chapters.title: When the Choir Sings
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, closing with Tam's epilogue-voice. Yara stays behind as the anchor while Tam and the freed captives pass through; the choir's song restores Vessany to the map, and Cassian turns his testimony against the crown. Emotional beat: sorrow braided with triumph—belonging won at the cost of leaving.
